Team —

Quick heads-up: finance needs a cleaned-up committed forecast for Q4 by EOD Monday (09/21). I ran the preliminary pass and flagged ~18 accounts with missing stage updates or no confirmed ARR. The list includes several medium-size renewals that are currently uncommitted but show strong usage (see Acme Corp).

Please do the following today:
- Each AE/owner must update SFDC "Commit Stage" and add a short one-line rationale for any account still "At Risk".
- For any account with >$50k ARR and no verbal commit, mark as "Escalate" and copy CSM on the thread.
- Attach any signed PO/DocuSign links to the HubSpot deal (use the related_links above for quick reference).

I've attached a working spreadsheet with the fields finance will consume. Fill the "Likely" column and flag any dependency (procurement, legal redlines, PO delay).

I'll run a second pass Monday morning and will escalate top-5 risks to leadership if we don't have concrete commit plans.

Thanks — keep updates tight (one-line per account).

Hannah Schmitt

Can your legal confirm the redline below is acceptable or propose the exact language by EOD Monday 9/21? If timing is tight, we can provide a temporary 2-week extension so service continuity is uninterrupted while legal finalizes the contract. Please let us know which you prefer.

Brightline Health (Daniel): procurement told our AE that the approval window opens 10/01. To expedite, we can issue a pre-approved invoice and Net-60 terms. Would that help your internal procurement calendar?

Action items (owners & deadlines):
- Karen / Acme legal: confirm retention clause or provide language — due 2026-09-21 EOD.
- Daniel / Brightline procurement: confirm if Net-60/pre-approved invoice works — due 2026-09-21 EOD.
- Ben (AE): attach any PO drafts or DocuSign links to the HubSpot deal.
- Marissa (CS): schedule joint AE+CS customer call for Acme Monday afternoon (target window: 2–4pm PT).

Finance will treat accounts without the above confirmations as uncommitted for Q4. If we get confirmations, we'll move Acme from "At Risk" to "Committed" in the forecast.
